title: Promise only what later lessons keep
statement: A lesson's promises about what comes next must hold in the lessons that follow; reword one they don't keep as something the learner will do.
example: Each of three lessons' closing words was used 57 to 59 times in its own lesson and 0 times in the lessons after.
detail: A simulated review round found that three lessons' closing screens promise the lesson's word will come along, and counts showed the words used 59, 57 and 57 times in their own lessons and 0 times in the lessons after; approved reference lessons showed the same shape. An earlier smoke audit had checked each 'next time' line against the following lesson and found them true, though one automated check wrongly assumed the last lesson in scope had no next lesson. The round's clean fix is to reword the line so it promises the learner will keep using the word, which is true and within the lesson's control.
against: It was kept as accepted exposure, partly because approved reference lessons do the same and the line "is not a stem, an option, an answer or any scored interaction, so no student ever gets a question wrong or a rail blocked because of it" (REGISTER-2026-09-15.md line 95).

evidence.quote: Each lesson's closing receipt explicitly promises the target word will continue ('Your word is coming with us: <word>')
That single-word, 0%-recurrence shape is the exact shape the finding calls out in L4 (enchanting, 59 in L4, 0 in L5-L7), L5 (menacing, 57 in L5, 0 after) and L6 (merciless, 57 in L6, 0 in L7)
the clean version is to reword the receipt so it promises the child will keep using the word, which is true and within our control, instead of implying the story will repeat it.
It is not a stem, an option, an answer or any scored interaction, so no student ever gets a question wrong or a rail blocked because of it
**Forward references in wrap text**, verified true of the following lesson:
an automated check assumed the last lesson in scope should have no forward pointer.
